proposals.title: Public-map frontier progress with explicit command phases
proposals.trigger: Every native NetHack observation, especially unchanged level or a pending command prompt.
procedure: Read the message before planning: a direction, item-letter, yes/no, menu or continuation prompt must be answered in that mode. Do not issue a fresh movement or inventory command into a pending prompt. The text cursor during a prompt is not the hero position; locate @ in the map.

From the public ASCII map, maintain current level, hero square, connected walkable region, observed downstairs, unexplored frontier exits, and confirmed blocked edges. Blank/unseen cells are not proven walkable. Use only relative directions admitted by the native action vocabulary.

Prioritize a known reachable downstairs. Trace a connected route on the actual map. Move along that route with single steps near doors, monsters or uncertain boundaries; use a far direction only along a visibly clear corridor, and verify displacement afterward.

If no downstairs is known, pursue one unvisited reachable frontier until it is explored or disproved. After a wall/solid-stone/no-displacement message, mark that exact local edge blocked and choose another reachable route. Do not alternate already-failed directions or revisit the start room without a remaining frontier there.

When a closed door blocks a useful frontier, stand orthogonally adjacent, open it and answer the direction prompt. Only if locked and this route is useful, kick with the correct follow-up direction. Avoid spending turns unlocking a door whose far side is already reachable by an open path.

If all visible frontiers are exhausted, search a small bounded number of turns at plausible dead ends or room-wall gaps, then move to a different candidate. Measure progress by new map cells, new reachable exits or deeper level, not movement count.

At low HP disengage through mapped safe squares before inventory healing or recovery. Prefer healing with verified inventory items over praying in melee. Read hunger and status each turn; avoid discretionary fights, repeated pickups and fountains that do not serve the objective.
invariants: No fixed map coordinates, object identifiers, seeded route or hidden state.
Never interpret turn count, survival, depth or partial progression as native success.
successSignals: Native environment confirms the task success condition.
failureSignals: Repeated action without the predicted public effect.
recovery: Recompute from current public feedback; do not replay a failed action unchanged.
